short: The Turco-Mongol conqueror who ruled from Delhi to Ankara and never called himself khan.
full:
Timur was born in the 1330s near Kesh in Transoxiana, into the Barlas, a Turkic clan of Mongol descent, and took a wound in his youth that left him lame — Timur-i Lang, Tamerlane. He fought his way up through the warlord politics of the broken western Chagatai realm, turned on his ally and brother-in-law Amir Husayn, and was proclaimed sovereign at Balkh on 9 April 1370. Not being a descendant of Genghis Khan, he could not take the title of khan. He ruled instead as amir in the name of a Chagatayid figurehead and married the Genghisid princess Saray Mulk Khanum, which entitled him to the style gurkani, son-in-law of the imperial house.

For thirty-five years he campaigned almost without pause: Persia, Georgia, the Golden Horde's cities on the Volga, Delhi in 1398, Aleppo, Damascus and Baghdad in 1401, the Ottomans at Ankara in 1402. Resisting cities were destroyed and their populations killed; their craftsmen were deported to Samarkand to build his capital. He died at Otrar in February 1405, marching in winter on Ming China.
